The patch changes the cast of of_device_get_match_data() to (uintptr_t) before converting to enum mxcmci_type, eliminating a clang -Wvoid-pointer-to-enum-cast warning in the mxcmmc driver.
The patch extends can_changelink() to also check can_priv::bitrate_const, enabling netlink configuration of CAN devices with fixed bit rates without requiring a dummy do_set_bittiming callback.
The patch adds a cleanup call on the error path of xhci_alloc_stream_info() to free the previously allocated stream_ctx_array, eliminating a memory leak in the XHCI host driver.
Adds a NULL‑pointer check after ioremap() in the ray_cs driver, validating local->sram and related pointers before use to avoid later dev_dbg on a NULL address.

The patch changes vsock_connect() to use mod_delayed_work() when the connect work is already pending and adds a sock_put() to balance the extra sock_hold, eliminating a memory leak reported by syzbot.
The commit rewrites the Atmel/Microchip I2C device tree binding from the old .txt format to a JSON‑schema representation, updating documentation to the new DT schema standard.
The patch moves the LCOUNT definition from implementation code into the Intel soundwire header, centralising it for clarity.
The patch updates habanalabs' map_block() to set the block‑id handle only when get_hw_block_id() succeeds, preventing a handle of 0 from being returned on failure.
The patch adds a missing WARN_ON validation for the VF pointer in ice_vsi_rebuild, fixing a kernel panic that occurred when resetting virtual functions.
The patch deletes the unused DMA‑32 fallback path in the hisi_sas SCSI driver, because dma_set_mask() with a 64‑bit mask never fails when dev->dma_mask is set, making the 32‑bit fallback redundant.

The patch updates the armada_37xx watchdog driver so that its .set_timeout callback also writes the new timeout value to counter 1, which .ping does not modify, ensuring ioctl(WDIOC_SETTIMEOUT) correctly changes the watchdog timeout.
The patch deletes the .is_enabled field from PRCMU clock drivers because the generic clock core already maintains a software enable count, removing redundant state.
The patch reorganizes riscv memory‑init code to place the pt_ops macro inside the CONFIG_XIP_KERNEL conditional and groups XIP‑only definitions, reducing scattered #ifdef CONFIG_XIP_KERNEL usage.
The patch relaxes the restriction on changing the SCSI target driver database root directory, allowing the change only when no devices are registered, fixing a usability limitation.

The patch adds calls to remove_kprobe_event_legacy() on error paths after add_kprobe_event_legacy() or attach_perf_event_opts(), ensuring stale kprobe events are cleaned up when livepatch and kprobe coexist.
The commit adds support for the MediaTek mt8186 System Control Processor (SCP) in the remoteproc driver, enabling the kernel to manage this co‑processor on mt8186 platforms.
The patch adds module parameters to the speakup_dummy driver so default driver settings can be specified at boot time, enabling configuration via module options instead of post‑boot sysfs writes.
Adds the legacy compatible string 'riscv,clint0' to the sifive,clint dt-binding so that QEMU‑generated device trees pass dt‑validate.

The patch updates swiotlb_max_mapping_size() to include the device's minimum alignment mask, fixing the max DMA mapping size calculation. This resolves boot failures on Hyper‑V Isolation VMs where offsets prevented finding a suitable bounce buffer.
The patch switches the Habana Labs CB flow to the new unified memory manager, adds required code for the flow, and removes the previous memory management implementation.

The patch modifies vmbus_request_addr() to return VMBUS_RQST_ERROR when the transaction ID is zero, preventing a NULL dereference in netvsc_send_completion() and making zero‑ID handling consistent with Hyper‑V semantics.
The commit updates the imx-jpeg driver to handle source changes within a function, enabling dynamic resolution changes at runtime.

The patch changes bpf_selem_alloc to use copy_map_value instead of memcpy, preventing the user‑supplied spin‑lock field from overwriting the zero‑initialized lock in map values for inode_storage, sk_storage, and task_storage maps.

The patch fixes a race in MPTCP's handling of consecutive ADD_ADDR options by caching the remote address earlier and consistently using the cached value after releasing the path manager lock, preventing overwriting.

The commit separates the device‑tree binding schema for Synopsys DW uMCTL2 DDR controllers from the Zynq A05 DDRC controller, updating the synopsys,ddrc-ecc.yaml and related documentation to reflect the different CSR layout and lack of IRQ support.
The patch modifies the Rockchip device‑tree for the ROCK Pi 4 series to set the I2S1 node status to “disabled”, ensuring the pins on the 40‑pin header stay in their default GPIO mode.
Adds clock and reset definitions for the ADC block in the Renesas r9a07g043 CPG driver, enabling the driver to manage ADC clocks and resets.
The patch deletes the declaration and assignment of the variable 'mdss' in drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_drv.c because the code that used it was removed, eliminating a clang ‘set but not used’ warning.

The patch changes tcp_v4_rcv() to call kfree_skb_reason() instead of kfree_skb(), supplying explicit drop reasons (NO_SOCKET, PKT_TOO_SMALL, TCP_CSUM, TCP_FILTER) so that freed‑skb trace events include the cause.

The patch deletes an obsolete comment and an unnecessary overflow check in the writeback code, relying on a prior fix that guarantees the variable cannot be negative or overflow, thus simplifying the implementation.
Updates the MAINTAINERS file to correct the reference to the Mediatek JPEG driver yaml files and expands the entry to include the encoder, fixing the get_maintainer script warning.
The patch modifies xfs_buf_incore() to return an error code and place the buffer in an output parameter, aligning it with other XFS buffer APIs for consistent usage.

The patch adjusts the DSC slice‑reset logic in the AMD DRM driver so that when neither the minimum nor maximum slice can accommodate the required pixel clock, DSC is correctly disabled instead of incorrectly allowing a max slice.
The patch adds clock and reset definitions for PWM channels 8‑14 in the Renesas r9a09g011 CPG driver, marks the shared APB clock as critical, and documents Linux usage restrictions.

The patch corrects MTU handling in the lan966x driver: it reads the maximum MTU from hardware (including L2 header and FCS) and adjusts skb allocation to account for skb_shared_info, preventing allocation failures when frames fill a page.
Adds bookkeeping to enable the host to unwind the hypervisor stack in non‑protected nVHE mode on arm64, storing the unwind start point and address translation data for later use.
The commit corrects a misspelled word in the error log printed when devm_snd_dmaengine_pcm_register() fails in the Microchip SPDIF receiver driver.
The patch sets fb_modifiers_not_supported in the vkms driver so AMDGPU stops using framebuffer modifiers, fixing GDM3 start failures on virtual displays.
Fixes Chinese documentation translation for the devicetree usage-model, keeping the term "machine_desc" untranslated.
Adds a helper function in the pmbus hwmon driver to test whether a block‑type register exists, because existing checks fail when PEC is enabled.
The patch replaces the multiline macro vt6655_mac_word_reg_bits_off in the vt6655 driver with an equivalent static inline function, because checkpatch rejects multiline macros.
Adjusts sysfs-fs-erofs ABI documentation to correct Sphinx formatting errors (indentation and block quote issues), allowing documentation to build without warnings.
The patch updates the Realtek rtw89 8852c driver to add extra initialization for BA CAM version 1 and adjust the H2C payload format, ensuring correct Block Ack CAM setup.
The commit only adjusts whitespace indentation in the dcn32_hwseq.c file to resolve a smatch warning, without altering any logic or functionality.

The patch updates the jz4740‑i2s ASoC driver to use separate TX and RX FIFO flush bits when available, flushing each FIFO independently before the active‑stream check, and fixes the previous behavior where only the TX flush bit was set, leaving RX unflushed on newer SoCs.
Updates the Qualcomm SM6350‑Lena device‑tree to enable QUP and GPI DMA controllers, making those DMA engines usable and preparing the board for functional I2C nodes.
Adds PCI IDs for Intel Raptor Lake PCH‑S LPSS so the driver can recognize the new hardware.
The patch deletes a duplicated word 'to' from a comment in the crypto n2 driver, cleaning up documentation without changing any code behavior.
The patch adds explicit DSD mode handling for the Accuphase DAC-60 USB audio device, enabling native DSD up to DSD256 by selecting the correct alternate setting.
Adds support for the VCN 4.0 IP block in the amdgpu DRM driver, implementing its initialization and decoder/encoder ring functions to enable the new hardware capability.
Adds EXPORT_SYMBOL for MediaTek VCodec decoder power‑management functions so they are visible to other modules when the decoder is built as a loadable module.
Adds READ_ONCE() around accesses to net->ipv4.sysctl_igmp_qrv to stop concurrent modifications causing data races in IGMP handling.
Adds a boolean rx_timeout variable in the 8250 DW driver IRQ path to make the timeout condition explicit; no functional change.
Adds proper error checking after calling nvmem_device_find in the PTP OCP driver, ensuring IS_ERR() is handled before using the pointer.

The patch renames the kernel macro for ID_AA64MMFR2_EL1.VARange to match the ARM specification naming, aligning kernel code with DDI0487H.a. It only updates identifiers, with no functional behavior change.
The patch updates comments in the rzg2l thermal driver: replaces an unclear phrase with a clearer one, corrects a typo, and moves the opening comment delimiter to its own line to follow coding style.
The patch removes a duplicated "the" in a comment on line 807 of powerpc/pseries/vas, fixing a typo without changing any code logic.
The patch deletes the unused variable cnt from recv_func in the r8188eu driver, cleaning up dead code.

Adds a check in release_swfw_sync for failure to acquire the hardware semaphore; on failure (e.g., surprise‑removed hardware) it logs an error and exits, preventing the previously possible infinite loop.

The patch modifies generic_map_delete_batch() to call maybe_wait_bpf_programs() only once after processing the entire batch, removing repeated synchronize_rcu() barriers as indicated by the function comment.

The patch rewrites the KVM self‑test state_test to create a single vCPU via vm_create_with_one_vcpu()/vm_recreate_with_one_vcpu(), passes a struct kvm_vcpu instead of a global VCPU_ID, changes the vCPU ID from 5 to 0, and switches to vcpu_run().

The patch replaces CONFIG_PM_SLEEP compile‑time guards in the vf610 IIO DAC driver with calls to pm_sleep_ptr(), letting the compiler drop the code when sleep support is disabled, simplifying the code and avoiding #ifdef usage.
The patch updates the copyright year range in the test files of the maple_tree subsystem, extending the span to include the current development year. No code logic is altered.
The patch updates the rc5t583 multi-function device driver to use the newer i2c .probe_new() callback instead of the older .probe, removing the unused i2c_device_id argument.
The patch adds an early‑return when vchiq_get_state receives a NULL pointer, avoiding a dereference and cleaning up the code for better readability.
Relocates efi32_pe_entry() from head_64.S into the .text section so it can later be compiled as a separate unit.
The patch moves two CEC register constant definitions from the public header adv7511.h into the source file adv7511_cec.c, eliminating unused‑variable warnings when the CEC driver option is disabled.
The patch modifies the Qualcomm SM6350 display clock driver, adding the CLK_OPS_PARENT_ENABLE flag to pixel and byte clock sources so that the set_rate operation can succeed.
The patch updates the pcm3168a ASoC driver to replace legacy bus‑clock defines with the newer ASoC DAI format terminology, aligning the code with current kernel conventions.

The patch adds a runtime validation that the number of IPA commands in a transaction does not exceed the TLV FIFO capacity, by passing a flag to gsi_channel_data_valid() and checking channel direction, using a local variable for command data.

The patch removes a non‑bit‑field member that precedes a bit‑field in a packed struct used by inside‑secure, eliminating unwanted padding that altered the struct size and broke zero‑initialisation and configuration calculations.

The patch fixes a bug where moving VCAP TCAM entries rewrites stale hit counters back to hardware, causing inflated statistics. It adds a read of the current counter into a temporary stats field before migration, ensuring counters are cleared correctly.
The patch deletes a conditional check for IS_SWAPFILE in the NFS code because the macro is always defined, eliminating dead code.
The patch corrects tps65219_set_bypass to rely on the regulator's .is_enabled() return value instead of testing .enable, and removes an unused ret variable, fixing incorrect enable-state detection.
Adds a transaction ID to the IPA driver to record the first completed but unpolled transaction, updates the ID during NAPI polling, and includes temporary consistency warnings that are later removed.
Deletes the unused tstamp pointer from mlx5e_txqsq after timestamp handling was moved to the core driver, cleaning up dead code in the mlx5e network driver.
The commit changes nxp-nci I2C handling to stop printing a wrong header length mismatch message when the I2C call fails, returning only the error code.
Adds device‑tree bindings so the WCN6750 Wi‑Fi chip can use Wake‑on‑Wireless (WoW) via the ath11k driver.

The patch replaces the use of the global ARCH_NR_GPIOS constant in the gpio‑aggregator driver with a locally defined macro (512) for the maximum number of GPIOs that can be aggregated, limiting the parser to a fixed size instead of the system‑wide limit.
The commit re-formats comment blocks in the r8188eu driver to follow the drivers/net coding style, ensuring consistency before the driver moves out of staging.
The commit adds a new device‑tree binding file describing the Renesas RZ/G2L interrupt controller, enabling the kernel to recognize this hardware in DT.
The patch changes the definition of PS_RDY_CHECK in the r8188eu driver to use the bool type, reflecting that the function returns true or false.
Adds a guard in gfs2_glock_dq() to verify a GL_ASYNC glock holder hasn't already been removed, preventing a race where asynchronous dequeue and explicit cancel could dequeue the holder twice.
The patch removes the driver‑specific yesno() helper and replaces its usage with the generic str_yes_no() from linux/string_helpers.h, updating includes accordingly.
The patch adds a validation to prevent the imx‑jpeg driver from using an invalid slot index (default MXC_MAX_SLOTS) when JPEG parsing fails, avoiding out‑of‑bounds array access and kernel panic.
Updates the ARM dt-bindings YAML file by adding compatible strings for DH electronics i.MX8M Plus DHCOM and PDK2 boards, documenting them as supported SoM/evaluation boards.
The patch fixes translate_desc() in the vhost driver by saving the 'last' parameter before incrementing addr, keeping the range end constant for vhost_iotlb_itree_first() calls.
Adds a guard in lib/cmdline's next_arg so args[i-1] is accessed only when i>0, preventing an out‑of‑bounds read that caused a kernel page fault when parsing arguments with stray quotes.
The patch reorders functions and variables in the via686a hwmon driver to eliminate four unnecessary forward declarations of static symbols, improving code organization without changing behavior.

The patch modifies acpi_processor_get_platform_limit() to compare the new _PPC value with the previously stored one and only update the frequency QoS request when it differs; it also validates the state count before storing and sets the default no‑limit QoS to FREQ_QOS_MAX_DEFAULT_VALUE.
The patch removes the build‑system logic that forced head.o to be linked first on arm64, relying on the linker script’s .head.text placement instead.
The patch replaces hard‑coded RAS DES PCIe capability offsets in the Tegra194 PCI driver with code that discovers the offset at runtime for each controller.
Adds a per‑frontend pause flag and changes the backend state machine so that when all active streams are paused the backend transitions to PAUSE instead of STOP, improving resource management.
Adds kernel support to record each unloaded module that taints the kernel, keeping a count and showing them in module listings; feature disabled by default.

The patch adds a lockdown check to the /proc/powerpc/ofdt interface, rejecting device‑tree modifications from untrusted user space when the kernel is locked down, thereby preventing misuse of the interface for arbitrary physical address writes.

Updates ADI ASoC drivers to use the new legacy_dai_naming flag (opt‑out) instead of the previous non_legacy_dai_naming opt‑in flag, aligning the code with the newer naming convention for CPU‑side DAIs.
The patch changes ptp_ocp memory allocation from kzalloc(x*y) to kcalloc(y, x) to use kcalloc's overflow checks, improving safety without altering functionality.
The patch removes the regs member from the coredump_params structure because its value is always the current task's pt_regs, making the field redundant.
Adds a dma_release_channel() call in the probe error path of sun4i-emac driver to correctly free a DMA channel obtained in emac_configure_dma() when probing fails.
The patch changes btrfs_ioctl to obtain the inode from the file descriptor and reuse it for callbacks instead of creating a new one, simplifying inode handling.
The patch replaces a hand‑rolled implementation of device_get_match_data() in acpi_smbus_cmi_add() with the standard helper, cleaning up the i2c/scmi driver code.
Adds a helper rdev_mdlock_deref() that wraps rcu_dereference_protected() for rdev/replacement pointers accessed while mddev_lock is held, to silence sparse warnings and document proper RCU usage.
Adds handling of GTP_ECHO_REQ in the GTP driver, sending GTP_ECHO_RSP with recovery IE and appropriate restart counter, bringing the device into compliance with the GTP spec.
Adds a guard to verify hdev is non‑NULL before accessing hdev->name in bt_dev_info/warn/err/dbg, preventing a null‑pointer dereference that caused kernel errors.

The patch replaces calls to cpumask_next_* with cpumask_first_* where the start index is -1 (i.e., beginning of mask) and adds a new helper cpumask_first_zero() to provide equivalent functionality, improving efficiency and simplifying code.
The commit marks the Clevo‑mail LED driver as broken because it uses brightness to control blink rate, which is unconventional, and notes that a proper interface fix is pending.
The patch checks the result of a BSS lookup; if it is an error pointer, it replaces it with NULL to avoid freeing an invalid pointer.
The patch adjusts the Aquantia PHY driver to stop advertising 2.5G/5G speeds when the interface is limited to 1 Gbps, clearing default advertisement bits during autonegotiation.

The patch adds an rcu_read_lock and takes a reference on the real device in bond_ethtool_get_ts_info(), fixing a crash that occurs when the function is invoked via setsockopt without holding RCU protection.
The patch adds logging for the GPIO and DMIC quirks in the Intel SOF ES8336 ASoC driver, extending the existing SSP quirk log so all quirks are reported.
The patch renames the variables maxpctksize and maxpcktsize to wMaxPacketSize in the USB gadget UAC2 driver to make the spelling consistent.

The patch modifies perf's data conversion to JSON so that tracepoint (probe) variables are emitted as name/value pairs using tep_print_field, enabling fields like __probe_ip and query_string_string in the JSON output.
The patch corrects misspelled words in pr_warn and pr_debug messages within the nvmet-auth driver, updating the literal strings to proper spelling without altering logic or behavior.
Edits a source file in the AMD DRM driver to correct a duplicated word in a comment, changing 'the the' to 'the'.

The patch refactors conv_uni_to_pc() in the consolemap code: it stores vc_uni_pagedir_loc in a local variable, adds a NULL check, splits a large conditional into smaller ones, and removes an unnecessary newline, making the function more readable.
The commit updates the MAINTAINERS file to add Paul Kocialkowski as the maintainer for the Allwinner A31 MIPI CSI-2 bridge media driver, with appropriate sign‑offs.

The patch adds a device‑specific override in the uvcvideo driver to restrict the power line frequency control for Chicony Easycamera models that implement it incorrectly, preventing the driver from exposing a broken control.

The patch corrects HDMI ODM combine mode handling in the AMD DRM driver. It stops false detection of mode changes, removes unnecessary stream reprogramming, and enforces a static ODM policy for HDMI TMDS/FRL on DCN32, eliminating intermittent black‑screen failures.

The patch removes the unit address from the panel endpoint node in the am335x device‑tree, because the endpoint should not have a unit address and the previous form caused a ‘reg is a required property’ error during DTS validation.

The patch changes the Hisilicon DRM driver to initialize on‑stack drm_mode structures using drm_mode_init() instead of manual initialization, ensuring the list head is properly set and eliminating leftover stack data.

The patch changes i915 display power code to stop using raw uncore register accesses and instead call the intel_de_* accessor functions, consolidating register I/O through the driver’s abstraction layer.

The commit adds runtime checks in the AMDGPU discovery code to compare the number of VCN and SDMA instances reported by firmware with the maximum supported by the driver structures, aborting if the firmware exceeds those limits.
The patch modifies the s390 exception‑table handling so that the amode31 extable is sorted before the early program‑check handler runs, ensuring early program checks can locate their entries.

The patch removes the reset_resume callback in the xpad wireless driver so the USB core rebinds the device after suspend/resume, preventing a hung URB that broke LED control and force‑feedback, restoring correct behavior on resume.
The patch makes fb_modesetting_disabled() a static‑inline function in the header, removing multiple definition linker errors when compiled into fbmon.o and fbmem.o.
The commit extends the lan743x network driver to handle Clause‑45 MDIO PHY management, enabling communication with PHYs using the Clause‑45 protocol.
Adds a new tools/include/pfn.h stub header with definitions needed by test code, without altering existing functionality.

The patch removes calls to acpi_video_set_dmi_backtype_type() in the toshiba_acpi driver and adds DMI quirks for two models with transflective displays, preventing premature unregistration of the acpi_video backlight and the resulting udev race.

The patch deletes the driver’s call to the dtim_assoc IOVAR, which always fails because recent firmware no longer supports it, stopping the repeated “wl dtim_assoc failed (-52)” messages after a roam.

The patch replaces BUG_ON() with WARN_ON_ONCE() in signal handling, so that unexpected conditions are logged but execution continues, avoiding kernel panic while holding core locks and improving debuggability.

The patch deletes three redundant variable initializations (bPacketMatchBSSID, bPacketToSelf, bPacketBeacon) in update_recvframe_phyinfo_88e of the r8188eu driver, as they are overwritten before any use.
The patch rewrites shmem_read_mapping_page_gfp() to call shmem_get_folio_gfp(), removing extra compound_head() calls and streamlining shared‑memory page handling.

Adds a check on the NTFS BOOT sectors_per_clusters field: if it encodes a shift value larger than allowed (cluster size >2 MiB) the code returns -EINVAL, avoiding negative or out‑of‑range shifts that caused a UBSAN error.

The patch removes the call to pfn_to_page from kasan_early_init on RISC‑V when CONFIG_KASAN and CONFIG_SPARSEMEM are enabled but CONFIG_SPARSE_VMEMMAP is disabled, preventing a null mem_section dereference before sparse_init runs.

The patch modifies the dpaa2‑eth driver to reuse a scatter‑gather (S/G) table cache for the normal transmission path, enlarging the cached buffers and replacing per‑packet allocations with get/recycle helper calls, thus avoiding repeated allocations and frees.
The commit updates the dt‑bindings maintainer entry, replacing the previous email with Krzysztof Kozlowski’s @kernel.org address in the MAINTAINERS file.
The commit extends the qcom,gsi-loader device‑tree property with a new enum value "skip", indicating that GSI firmware is already loaded and should not be loaded by AP or modem.

The commit changes the Qualcomm SDM630 device‑tree description to use MMIO for the TCSR mutex instead of a syscon regmap, aligning the binding with the hardware's dedicated address space and satisfying DT schema checks.

The patch corrects the interrupt exit path on PowerPC 64-bit systems so that when returning to a soft-masked (irqs-disabled) context it no longer clears the hard-mask flag, preventing loss of pending soft-masked IRQs, and adds a clarifying comment.

The patch marks all I/O master CPUs on LoongArch as non‑hotpluggable (hotpluggable=0) and stops the kernel from creating the /sys/.../online sysfs file for them, avoiding confusion for user‑space tools.
The patch deletes the unused variable 'last' from the ia64 remove_siblinginfo() function, eliminating dead code and simplifying the function.

The commit updates the arm64 selftest Makefile to use TEST_GEN_PROGS_EXTENDED instead of TEST_PROGS_EXTENDED, aligning with kselftest lib.mk's default target for building generated test programs while keeping script‑based tests unchanged.
Adds rollback in fbcon_do_set_font() so that if vc_resize() fails while changing font size, the font state is restored, preventing inconsistent state and page faults reported by syzbot.
Adds a dt-binding property 'power-domains' for MediaTek video encoder nodes, documenting that the encoder may depend on a power domain.
The commit changes the logging level for power and thermal envelope events in the Gaudi2 driver, treating them as informational messages instead of warnings or errors.
Updates DT binding files for Hirschmann/Hellcreek network devices to use absolute paths for referenced schemas, following preferred style.
Adds EXPORT_SYMBOL macros for mt6358 driver functions so they are visible to other modules, fixing undefined symbol errors when the driver is built as a module.
Reorders fields in the LTTPR UHBR link‑rate support structure to follow the DP2.0 specification, updating the driver code accordingly.
The patch modifies the wcd9335 ASoC driver to check if the slimbus mux value actually changes; if not, it returns early, stopping unnecessary event notifications that were previously always reported.

The patch moves acquisition of card->lock earlier in fw_core_handle_bus_reset so that accesses to card->local_node and card->bm_retries are protected, and removes redundant lock acquisition inside fw_destroy_nodes callsites, adding a comment about required locking.

The patch moves the _set_policy function into the chip_ops structure for the rtw89 driver, allowing RTL8852C to define additional coexistence policies (e.g., DBCC, multi‑role, TDMA) required by its firmware.
The patch deletes an unused assignment to the variable 'negative' in the ad2s1210 IIO driver, eliminating a dead‑store warning from clang static analysis.
The patch changes the octeontx2 PF driver to forward AF replies directly to the VF, preserving the error code set by AF instead of discarding it, so the VF can handle those errors.
The patch removes an obsolete flags check for CHIP_IP_DISCOVERY in the amdgpu DRM driver because IP‑based discovery is now always available.

The patch modifies the dw_hdmi bridge driver to send General Control Packets only when the connected sink supports Deep Color, disabling automatic GCP for 24‑bit mode on non‑Deep‑Color sinks, aligning behavior with HDMI 1.4b spec.
The patch modifies ARM IRQ entry assembly to stop using register R9, preserving it for the entry/exit code that relies on its value.
Updates the AMD DRM driver to set the VSC packet revision to rev2 for PSR1, implementing the VSC packet rev4 required by the eDP 1.5 specification (PSRSU).
The commit modifies tools/tracing/Makefile to add, install, and clean rules for the rtla target, enabling the build system to compile and manage the rtla tracing utility.
Adds a device‑tree compatible entry for the PCA85073A RTC, mapping it to the existing PCF85063A driver because they share the same programming model, enabling the driver to bind to that hardware.
The patch updates the Chrome EC Type‑C driver to assign the correct parent pointer to USB‑PD objects representing a connected Type‑C partner, using the registration wrapper.
Adds device‑tree entries for an MMIO‑based MDIO multiplexer on the ls1043a‑qds board, defines a simple‑mfd compatible node, and connects Ethernet interfaces to the PHYs.
The patch adjusts the mt76 driver to ensure the IEEE80211_VHT_CAP_TX_ANTENNA_PATTERN and RX_ANTENNA_PATTERN flags are set during 6 GHz capability initialization, fixing missing antenna configuration.

Adds a gfp_t argument to convert_context() and its wrapper, letting callers pass GFP_KERNEL or GFP_ATOMIC, and updates callers so memory allocation inside the spin‑locked section uses GFP_ATOMIC, eliminating the BUG sleeping warning.

The patch registers a shutdown() callback for the WCN6750 Wi‑Fi device in the ath11k driver so that DMA stops before the SMMU driver is shut down, preventing SMMU translation faults on system power‑off.

The patch updates the Ocelot driver so that bridge port flag operations on the NPI port are forwarded to the analyzer block entry that represents the CPU port, enabling the Felix DSA driver to control flooding on its CPU port.
The commit updates the Qualcomm remoteproc DT binding documentation to include the msm8974 variant, noting an extra mss-supply property handled by a simple conditional.
The patch adds a guard in dc_submit_i2c_oem to check if the DDC pointer is NULL and aborts the operation, preventing a null‑pointer dereference.

The commit updates the fsl-lpuart device-tree binding header by deleting the i.MX8QM entry from the compatible enum, because that SoC’s UART is compatible with i.MX8QXP. This forces device tree nodes to list both compatible strings, relying on existing 'items' entry.

The patch changes i915_gem_context.link handling so the list entry is removed only after the final reference is released, fixing a general protection fault in i915_perf. It also corrects spin_lock usage.
Adds a helper that allocates MSI‑X vectors for virtual queues and configuration interrupts in the vDPA ifcvf driver, enabling proper interrupt handling for virtual devices.

The patch removes a snd_BUG_ON() check for a NULL port in snd_usbmidi_output_open(), because the NULL can occur with malformed descriptors and the driver already skips allocation; keeping the BUG_ON caused spurious kernel oops reported by syzbot.

The patch modifies the Sony laptop ACPI driver to skip probing the keyboard backlight when the 0x153 SNC handle lacks a dedicated probe address, preventing the probe from unintentionally turning the backlight off.

The patch limits 36‑bpp linebuffer usage to DCN display engines, keeping DCE engines at 30‑bpp to avoid dithering issues observed on DCE‑11.2, thereby restoring correct pixel passthrough for scientific applications.
The patch renames the inner variable in mac80211 airtime code to avoid shadowing the outer 'rate' variable, improving code clarity.

The patch updates x86/boot inline assembly to wrap literal address casts with absolute_pointer() macro, eliminating GCC 11/12 false‑positive -Warray-bounds warnings caused by treating literal pointers as NULL offsets.
The commit adds hardware definitions for LEDs and buttons of the Asus RTN-10U router to the BCM47XX MIPS driver, enabling support for this device.
The patch marks irq_chip structures used by pinctrl actions as immutable, removes an unnecessary copy, adds helper functions, and invokes gpiolib helpers to enforce the immutability flag.
Updates the i.MX8MP Phycore SOM device tree: disables unused LDO4 and enables LDO5, which supplies VSEL for the SD‑Card controller, matching the board's hardware design.

The patch updates the Microchip PIT64B timer driver to call mchp_pit64b_suspend() and mchp_pit64b_resume() for clock management during init/remove, removing explicit clk_prepare_disable/enable calls, and relies on state callbacks for clockevent timers.

The patch standardises how underscores and dots are added to UC filenames by moving delimiter handling into the concatenation macro, removing explicit prefixes and making the macro generate consistent filenames.
Adds snd_card_free() call in the probe error path of the sonicvibes ALSA driver via a helper, ensuring proper resource release before card registration.
Adds a dmaengine driver for the Apple ADMAC audio DMA controller present in Apple Silicon SoCs, integrating it into the kernel's DMA engine subsystem.
The patch changes the udl DRM driver to pass a rectangle structure directly to udl_handle_damage(), removing intermediate handling and simplifying the code path.
Adds additional self‑test cases for the BPF btf_dump utility to verify handling of padding edge cases, including handcrafted and fuzz‑generated inputs.
The patch adds a call to unregister_candev() in mcp251x_can_probe() when mcp251x_gpio_setup() fails, ensuring the CAN device is properly cleaned up on probe error.
Adjusts bullet list indentation in Documentation/ABI/testing/sysfs-class-thermal to match other files, removing a Sphinx warning about a list ending without a blank line.
The commit updates the verdin-imx8mp device tree for arm64, adding support for USB_1 over‑current detection by defining the USB_1_OC# pin as active‑low and removing its previous gpio_hog3 assignment.
The patch adds handling for the CMD_ERROR_EVENT in the kvaser_usb leaf driver, logging or reacting to an unexpected error command that indicates a driver malfunction.
The patch renames the macro definitions for the ID_AA64ISAR2_EL1 register to include the _EL1 suffix, aligning them with the convention used for other system registers; no code behavior is altered.
Updates egress rate‑limit handling for CN10K by correcting register burst fields and widening maxrate variable to 64‑bit, aligning driver with new hardware register format.
Replaces a BUG_ON check with WARN_ON in the sfc driver and adds recovery code, reducing fatal aborts and addressing a checkpatch warning.
The patch changes the uid_strings const array from a stack‑allocated variable to a static definition, moving it to read‑only data and shrinking the generated object code.
The patch defines a constant for the fixed value 0x6 and removes the unused UsbTxAggDescNum member from the hal_data_8188e structure in the r8188eu driver.
The patch changes uml_vector_default_bpf() to accept a const MAC address pointer, aligning with recent constification of MAC addresses and fixing compilation errors.

The commit renames the test‑mode TX antenna configuration from a chain‑mask to a unified antenna_mask for both band0 and band1, updating driver code to use the new field and eliminating the conversion when building firmware commands.

The patch ensures that when a page is split or migrated, its private pointer is cleared. It zeroes page->private after allocation and for tail pages, fixing cases where PG_private is cleared but folio->private remains non-NULL.
The patch corrects a spelling mistake in a comment within the ASoC AMD ACP driver, changing the typo to the proper word without altering code logic.
Adds Mediatek Ethernet driver PCS register definitions based on investigation, updating header constants to match hardware specifics.

The patch adds a kernel warning and updates comments in the fbdev hot‑unplug workaround for framebuffers lacking a device, noting that the workaround should no longer be needed now that OF framebuffers have platform devices.
The commit changes F2FS to treat a zoned block device as having a single uniform zone capacity, removing per‑zone capacity handling and simplifying space management.
The commit updates all source files to replace the GPLv2 boilerplate text with the SPDX identifier 'GPL-2.0-only', standardizing license declarations across the tree.
The patch deletes an unused declaration of sni_cpu_time_init() from the MIPS time code after previous commits removed all its calls, cleaning up dead code.
The patch raises the AMD DRM display compositor buffer size before clock updates to avoid P‑State hangs caused by the buffer not being programmed in time.
Adds a device‑tree node for the Mediatek MT6795 pinctrl controller, exposing it to the kernel while leaving pin configuration to machine‑specific DTS files.
The commit corrects misspelled identifiers and comments in the ath10k Wi‑Fi driver, based on codespell output. It only changes text, leaving runtime behavior unchanged.
The patch deletes a redundant resource‑null check in the c67x00 USB driver's remove() routine because the probe already validated the resource.
The commit updates KVM x86 documentation about MSR filtering, clarifying terminology, correcting an off‑by‑one range description, and removing redundant or inaccurate paragraphs.

The patch changes the memory‑management helper that extracts swap flags from a page to operate directly on a folio, eliminating an unnecessary page‑to‑folio conversion because the sole caller already works with a folio.
Updates the LRO state‑modify error string in the mlx5e driver, replacing the old specific text with a more generic name to improve diagnostic clarity.
Adds support for nested VMLOAD and VMSAVE instructions in KVM's x86 nSVM implementation, enabling proper handling when running multiple nested Linux guests.
The patch modifies the Cadence SoundWire driver to treat msg->buf as read‑only for write commands, preventing it from being overwritten and thus avoiding corruption of the caller's data buffer.
Adds a temporary struct device variable in the intel_soc_pmic_bxtwc driver to extend its usage and make the code cleaner.
The patch moves several local variables used in dml32_CalculateSwathAndDETConfiguration into a temporary dummy structure, lowering the function’s stack frame size.
The commit reorganizes the Chinese admin-guide documentation index and improves the HTML To‑do list formatting for better visual presentation.

The commit relocates the TSC‑ratio constants/definitions used by the SVM virtualization code from a source file into the svm.h header, aligning the implementation with the SVM specification and improving code organization.
Adds documentation for the Renesas RZ/G2UL USB2 PHY device‑tree bindings, noting it matches the RZ/G2L PHY and can use the existing compatible string.

The patch refactors the ltc2983 temperature driver to obtain configuration data via generic device properties instead of relying on OF, allocating a buffer for all values at once, thus making the driver work on non‑OF platforms.
Updates STM32 device‑tree to add an alternate pin‑mux option for DCMI pins, required for the AV96 board.
The commit reverts a previous change that fixed batched wait_cnt accounting in sbitmap because it caused CPU stalls and possible infinite loops, restoring the original behavior.
The patch deletes references to the q->qid field in the mt76 driver because the field is no longer used, cleaning up dead code.
The patch saves the device's base register before freeing the MMC host in moxart_remove() and uses that saved value instead of dereferencing the freed host pointer, eliminating a use‑after‑free bug.
The patch ensures the sta.mlo flag is set for stations using Multi‑Link Operation (MLO) in the mac80211 MLME code, correcting an omission introduced by earlier changes.
Adds minimal register set definitions for m68k, enabling ELF FDPIC loader core dump support; code is conditionally compiled only when that feature is needed.
The commit updates the imx319 I2C driver to set V4L2_CTRL_FLAG_MODIFY_LAYOUT on the flip control, ensuring the Bayer order change is correctly reported to V4L2.
The patch changes the return type of rnbd‑srv's process_msg_close function from int to void because it always returns 0, removing an unnecessary return value.
Adds support for the SBI v0.3 System Reset (SRST) extension in the RISC‑V KVM guest, enabling standard power‑off and reboot operations via the SBI interface.

The commit updates x86/Kconfig to enable 16‑byte NOP padding before every function, leveraging existing 16‑byte alignment to support software call‑stack tracking and kCFI/FineIBT, increasing .text size by ~5% without measurable performance loss.

The patch renames the clock identifier video_pll1 to video_pll in the i.MX8MN driver to match the reference manual and audio PLL naming, keeping old constants for backward compatibility and introducing no functional changes.

The patch replaces a custom ad‑hoc check for a single enabled CRTC in i9xx_update_wm() with the standard single_enabled_crtc() helper and removes an unnecessary variable, aligning the code with other legacy WM functions.

Adds a guard in the AMD DRM driver to verify a PSR panel has entered PSR before switching to MALL state, and prevents overwriting link settings when programming a phantom stream sharing the same link.
The patch modifies audit_init_parent() to accept a const‑qualified path pointer, updating its prototype and related call sites to enforce read‑only usage of the path argument.
Updates the tas2770 ASoC driver to accept mono audio streams, handling downmix and channel switching so the right channel index ranges 1‑2.
The patch changes the STM32 VREFBUF regulator driver to call pm_runtime_resume_and_get instead of pm_runtime_get_sync, simplifying the runtime‑PM handling.
The patch updates the Intel raw NAND driver to read the chip‑select line from the flash device's OF node (a child of the controller) instead of the controller node, fixing the hardware mapping.
The patch replaces XFS inode fork size macros with inline helper functions, removing shouty macros and adding type‑checked calls to improve safety and readability.

The patch corrects hci_read_buffer_size_sync to call the LE‑specific helper hci_le_read_buffer_size_sync instead of using the LE‑only opcode HCI_OP_LE_READ_BUFFER_SIZE_V2, fixing a bug where the wrong opcode was used.

Switches the efuse buffer in ReadAdapterInfo8188EU from a fixed 512‑byte stack array to a kmalloc‑allocated buffer, freeing it on exit, and drops the __aligned(4) qualifier because kmalloc already provides sufficient alignment.
The patch marks several functions in dcn32_hubbub.c as static because they are only used within that file, removing warnings about missing prototypes and limiting their visibility.

The patch changes the PTP OCP driver to compute which sysfs attribute groups need registration, creates them with sysfs_create_groups, and avoids calling sysfs_remove_group on groups that were never added, fixing a crash on detach.
The patch deletes the declaration of intel_gt_create_kobj() from the i915 GT driver because the function is never referenced, cleaning up dead code.
The patch edits the max9759 ASoC driver Kconfig to drop an unnecessary 'select GPIOLIB' line, making GPIO support optional and silencing spurious warnings during random configuration builds.

The patch introduces folio_batch_move_lru() and begins converting the LRU handling from pagevec structures to folio_batch structures, merging existing pagevec functions into new folio_batch equivalents.
The patch deletes the f2fs_lock_op call in f2fs_new_inode because the allocation routine does not need to block checkpoint and the related function already holds the necessary nat_tree_lock.
Adds a helper function is_subset to the perf cpumap code that returns true when the second cpumap is a subset of the first, enabling easier subset checks within the perf subsystem.
Adds explicit missing #include directives to the lynxpoint pinctrl driver and sorts all headers alphabetically, ensuring only directly used headers are included.
The patch deletes tcf_connmark_walker and tcf_connmark_search from the act_connmark scheduler and uses the generic walk/search function instead, removing duplicated code.
The patch updates the Nouveau driver for TU102 GPUs to correctly send the high 32 bits when initializing a 64‑bit software bundle, fixing a missing field that previously defaulted to zero.
The patch updates the rkvdec driver to call the newly added vb2_find_buffer helper, retrieving a vb2_buffer based on its timestamp instead of the previous method.
Adds unit tests for MCTP key/tag lookup logic, inserting a specific entry into key lists, sending a packet with particular header values, and verifying match/mismatch behavior.
Adds a manual snd_card_free() call in the cs46xx ALSA driver’s probe error path to correctly release resources before the card is registered, fixing a leak caused by devres cleanup ordering.
The patch replaces a manual error‑logging sequence in the mxsfb DRM driver with the generic dev_err_probe() helper, removing duplicated code and exposing a deferred‑device hint in sysfs.
The patch modifies bootmem to replace uses of page->freelist with page->index, because both hold the same bits but index is an integer, eliminating pointer casts.
Updates the sdw‑mockup ASoC driver to replace its manual hw_params‑to‑SoundWire config conversion with the generic snd_sdw_params_to_config helper, simplifying the code.
The patch adds a missing configfs_put() on the error path of configfs_create_dir() to correct the reference count, eliminating the memory leak reported by kmemleak.

The patch refactors xdp_do_redirect() to return more specific errno values: ENOMEM for allocation failures and ENOBUFS when the AF_XDP Rx ring is full, while keeping existing codes for other cases, enabling drivers to distinguish error causes.
The patch changes the NVMe PCI driver’s reset failure handling so that, instead of unbinding the driver, it simply shuts down the controller and leaves it in a dead state.
Adds unevaluatedProperties/additionalProperties=false to child node schemas in dt-bindings opp, tightening validation to allow only documented properties.
Adds a missing put_uid call in __io_sqe_files_scm() when no files are present, closing a memory leak in io_uring file registration.
Updates ARM crypto Kconfig for __cbc-aes-neonbs to SELECT generic CBC and AES implementations, providing a fallback so the algorithm can register correctly at boot.

Adds a runtime check in ASoC core to detect when the driver field of snd_ctl_card_info is set via the generic wrapping method, which can truncate names and cause clashes, and prints an error prompting driver developers to fix the initialization.
Adds a board configuration (adl_rt5682) for the Intel SOF driver to support the alc5682 headset codec on platforms without a speaker amplifier, connecting it to SSP0.

The patch removes the unused gfp_flags argument from null_alloc_page() in the null_blk driver, updates its sole caller null_insert_page() to rely on the default GFP_NOIO, and adjusts related code, eliminating a hard‑coded parameter.
Implements a minimal sysfs stub for DAMON, creating a directory hierarchy and 'nr' files so users can build monitoring contexts via sysfs instead of debugfs.
Adds a 'depends on NET' clause to INTEL_HFI_THERMAL Kconfig entry so that it respects the NET dependency required by THERMAL_NETLINK, eliminating a Kconfig warning and many build errors.

The patch corrects swapped bitmask definitions in the RX_DMA_GET_SPORT and RX_DMA_GET_SPORT_V2 macros of the MediaTek Ethernet SOC driver, ensuring each macro uses the proper mask for extracting the source port.

The patch corrects the prefetch calculation loop in the AMD DCN3.2 display driver so that after a failure the loop resets its local variables each iteration, preventing it from consuming the entire vstartup range.
Adds proper synchronization to roccat_read() to stop the race where a report buffer can be freed while being copied to userspace, eliminating a use‑after‑free condition.
The patch deletes the unused CONFIG_DRM_AMD_DC_DCN option from the amdgpu_dm directory, making the AMD display driver code OS‑agnostic and eliminating unnecessary conditional compilation.
The patch adjusts mac80211 DTIM handling so the DTIM period is stored in link->conf->dtim_period and not overwritten, while still preferring beacon data when available.
Adds the list_for_each_table_entry macro to proc sysctl code to traverse ctl_table more cleanly, improving readability and potential traversal efficiency.
The patch adjusts io_uring's multishot accept handling to drop pending accepts when the completion queue overflows, fixing ordering problems similar to the multishot poll case.
The patch restores correct speed configuration for CPU/DSA ports in mv88e6xxx by calling mv88e6xxx_get_caps() early, because mac_capabilities were previously zero, causing a default 10 Mbps setting.
The commit updates ath10k driver code to replace strlcpy with strscpy and adjusts a printf format to silence recent checkpatch warnings, without changing functionality.
Updates the it66121 device‑tree binding file to document audio‑related properties, enabling the bridge to be described with audio support in DT.
Adds a check in io_uring networking code to reject zerocopy sendmsg operations on sockets that do not support zerocopy, mirroring earlier handling for send requests.
The commit adds support for the ethtool --identify option in the NFP driver, enabling the NIC firmware to blink the panel LED when requested.
Adds device‑tree binding definitions for the Himax hx83112b touchscreen, providing the necessary property descriptions for this hardware.
The commit adds a regulator node and enables the PCIe 2 controller and its combphy in the quartz64-b device tree, providing hardware support for PCIe 2 on that board.

The patch separates nvme_kill_queues into two parts: one that marks all namespace disks dead and another that unquiesces I/O queues. The unquiescing is moved to callers, and the remaining function is renamed nvme_mark_namespaces_dead.

The patch removes an unnecessary condition that checks for Correctable Error (CE) status when querying RAS error addresses in the amdgpu driver, leaving only the Uncorrectable Error (UE) address query.

The patch resolves Sparse static‑analysis warnings in arch/powerpc/kernel/time.c by declaring decrementer_max in asm/time.h, adding linux/mc146818rtc.h for rtc_lock, removing duplicate rtc_lock definition, and moving dtl_consumer after including <asm/dtl.h>.
Replaces inline enable/disable code in the Merrifield GPIO driver with the generic str_enable_disable() helper, removing duplicated logic.
Adds a check for xeCJK.sty before loading it in the kerneldoc preamble, avoiding LaTeX errors on systems where the package is absent.

The patch replaces uses of the 16‑byte struct sockaddr with struct sockaddr_storage in NFS server structures and memcpy calls, aligning buffer sizes with the union member to stop fortify‑source overflow warnings.
The patch updates Btrfs code to use the self‑documenting macro OFFSET_MAX instead of INT_LIMIT(loff_t), improving readability of the maximum file offset constant.
The patch removes the obsolete of_gpio.h header from the zevio GPIO driver and updates the driver to use the standard of_* APIs and structures, adjusting calls accordingly.

The commit adjusts the compute unit (CU) masking logic for GFX10+ ASICs with work‑group processors, making the mask pairwise contiguous and round‑robin distributing CUs across shader engines to correctly handle WGP mode.

The patch replaces a custom implementation of delayed work cancellation in the max14656 power supply driver with the kernel-provided devm_delayed_work_autocancel helper, reducing code size and leveraging device-managed cleanup.
Adds a hardware capability flag for ARM64 MTE asymmetric mode (FEAT_MTE3) so userspace can detect support via the hwcap mechanism.

The patch extracts combo PHY register definitions from the generic i915 register header into a dedicated header, limiting inclusion to files and platforms that actually need them, improving code organization.
The commit updates the Palmas MFD driver to replace manual match‑data extraction with the helper device_get_match_data(), simplifying the driver’s initialization code.
The patch updates the ptp_pch driver to replace custom 64‑bit I/O code with the kernel‑provided ioread64_hi_lo() and iowrite64_hi_lo() helpers, simplifying handling on 32‑bit platforms and buses.
The commit deletes the sx8 block driver files, removing support for an obscure hardware block device that has been unmaintained since 2005.
Updates the Qualcomm USB VBUS regulator DT binding by renaming the generic node from "dcdc" to "usb-vbus-regulator" and adjusting the example to match.
Adds the UNTRAIN_RET macro to the Xen entry on x86, making the return path go through UNTRAIN_RET to extend retpoline mitigation for Xen.
The patch deletes the unused <linux/gpio.h> include from the i2c/ccs driver, which already uses <linux/gpio/consumer.h>, cleaning up the source file.
Updates kbuild header_check to stop checking include/linux/cyclades.h, which now intentionally warns if included, so the test should not flag it.
The commit introduces a mechanism to override the device used for DMA mapping in the mt76 driver, enabling the WED driver to switch the PCI HIF to non‑coherent DMA when needed.

The patch renames the function btrfs_insert_file_extent() to btrfs_insert_hole_extent() throughout Btrfs code, because the function only inserts hole extents. It also drops unused parameters, updating all call sites accordingly.

The patch fixes a kmemleak in orangefs_prepare_debugfs_help_string by always freeing the allocated debug_help_string buffer when the module is removed or when free_debug_help_string changes, preventing the leaked 4 KB allocation.
The commit updates the Qualcomm ADSP remoteproc device tree binding to simplify interrupt constraints, removing the need for a separate optional interrupt entry.
The patch raises the GT reset‑failure timeout from 5 s to 60 s, delaying the device‑wedge action to allow more diagnostics and avoid premature failure.
The commit introduces handling of PTP timestamp interrupts in the sparx5 Ethernet driver, allowing the driver to read timestamps from the hardware FIFO during two‑step timestamping.
Adds a requires_cpu flag to perf stat for uncore events, separating them from the system_wide flag and ensuring they are bound to a specific CPU.
Adds kernel documentation strings for core domain fields in the Tegra PMC driver, enabling proper generation of documentation via kerneldoc.
The patch adds a NULL check after platform_get_resource() in the mt6397 RTC driver to avoid dereferencing a NULL pointer, fixing a crash scenario.
Renames the existing filter function group and related identifiers to include "vlan_" for clearer distinction from the upcoming QinQ filtering group, without changing functionality.
The patch deletes the now‑unused arch_kprobe_override_function() prototype from x86/kprobes after earlier changes eliminated all calls, cleaning up dead code.

The patch wraps the -mno-branch-likely flag in a cc-option wrapper for MIPS Loongson targets, so clang’s unused‑argument warning no longer triggers -Werror. It also moves the cc-option test into Kconfig, performing the check at configuration time and speeding up unchanged builds.
The patch changes platform code to call fwnode_irq_get_byname instead of of_irq_get_byname, allowing named interrupt lookup for devices described by ACPI as well as OF via the fwnode abstraction.
Adds a new helper function hda_codec_device_remove() to the Intel SOF ASoC HDA codec driver, separating removal logic between controller and codec components.
The commit adds the mmhub v3_0_1 hardware header files to the amdgpu DRM driver, updating definitions to match the newer hardware version.
The patch modifies ptp_ocp_verify() to use snprintf() instead of sprintf(), improving safety and readability of the formatting operation.
The patch rewrites devm_clk_hw_register_clkdev() to use devm_add_action_or_reset() instead of devres_alloc()/devres_add(), simplifying the implementation without altering behavior.
Adds runtime validation of the user-provided CQ counter offset in the habanalabs driver, checking the value in wait_for_interrupt and register_for_timestamp before use.
The patch updates the printf format for div_sel from %d to the correct specifier for a u32, matching the variable's unsigned 32‑bit type.
Adds support for additional TC flower filter keys to the Sparx5 IS2 VCAP, including IPv4/IPv6 addresses, fragments, ports, VLAN, TCP flags, IP TOS, and a 128‑bit keyfield API for IPv6.
The patch extends the meson-gpio IRQ driver to support Meson S4 SoCs, adding definitions for the larger set of GPIO IRQ lines and fixing build warnings.
Adds a new x86 CPU feature bit for AMD PerfMonV2, exposing CPUID leaf 0x80000022 bits so the kernel can detect and use the new performance monitoring capabilities.
The patch frees the rwi structure after a successful reset, eliminating a 32‑byte memory leak introduced by a prior commit that left the last rwi allocated.
The patch casts the return value of __fls to unsigned long in the Intel AVS ASoC driver because on arc, m68k and sparc __fls returns int, causing a %ld format warning that breaks the build.
The commit renames ice_sriov.c and its header to ice_vf_mbx.c to reflect that the file contains generic VF mailbox code, not SR-IOV specific, facilitating future Scalable IOV support.

The patch separates the existing cp_task field in f2fs_inode_info into cp_task (for IO accounting) and wb_task (to avoid deadlock), correcting mis‑classification of data‑flush IO as checkpoint IO when the data_flush mount option is enabled.

Adds a guard in ieee80211_tx_control_port() to skip __ieee80211_select_queue() when the hardware reports fewer than four TX queues, restoring correct queue mapping for non‑QoS drivers such as rt2500‑pci.
Adds driver support for the Multi‑Gigabit Ethernet (MGBE/XPCS) IP on NVIDIA Tegra234 SoCs to the stmmac network driver, enabling kernel interaction with this hardware.
Adds string representations for two missing IAVF state enums so debug prints show correct state names, fixing confusing log output.
The patch modifies perf inject to detect a kcore_dir in the input perf.data and copy that directory into the output, preserving kallsyms and related files for later analysis.
The patch updates the sun4i_can device tree binding to reference the newly added common CAN controller binding, aligning the documentation with the shared can-controller.yaml definition.
The commit moves Renesas PRR device‑tree binding files from the soc directory to a new hwinfo directory, grouping chip‑ID and SoC information under hwinfo.
The patch deletes an unnecessary cast to u8 when comparing two u8 fields (card_8192_version and IC_Cut) against the macro VERSION_8190_BD, simplifying the expression without altering functionality.
The patch deletes an unnecessary #include of linux/msi.h from the iommu/of driver source file, as the file does not use any symbols from that header.

The patch extends the GPMI raw NAND driver to handle NAND devices with OOB size larger than 1 KB by adding a BCH geometry selection algorithm that tries ECC strengths and optionally adds a separate ECC for metadata to keep the bad‑block marker inside data chunks.
The patch wraps Energy Model‑related functions in #ifdef CONFIG_ENERGY_MODEL guards, removing unused‑function warnings and avoiding unnecessary work when the Energy Model is disabled.
The patch initializes previously uninitialized variables and adds checks for possible ERR_PTR returns in octeontx2 driver files, eliminating smatch static analysis warnings.
Removes duplicate wake‑up interrupt definitions from the Exynos850 pin‑controller node in the device‑tree, correcting the placement according to the expected schema.
The patch adds interrupt configuration and handling support for the Micrel ksz9477 PHY driver, mirroring existing implementations for other Micrel PHYs.
Adds support for the t6000 DART hardware in the iommu io-pgtable-dart driver, handling its 42-bit PTE format and mandatory sub-page protection by configuring it to allow full-page access.
The patch updates scripts/checkpatch.pl to allow macros that expand to a 'case' statement, stopping the tool from flagging them as missing parentheses.

The patch replaces a manual size calculation in pwc_decompress() with the kernel’s struct_size() helper, eliminating the use of sizeof on a flexible struct and removing related sparse warnings, thereby preventing possible integer overflow and heap overflow.
The patch replaces calls to nodes_weight() with nodes_empty() in x86 code where only a presence test is needed, using early‑exit traversal for faster nodemask checks.
The commit adds a dma-channel-mask property to the Tegra GPCDMA device‑tree node and expands the interrupts list to cover all 32 channels, correcting the previous driver limitation to 31 channels.
Adds runtime checks when a KVM x86 vendor module loads, using updated KVM_X86_OP annotations to warn if any kvm_x86_ops members are incorrectly NULL, preventing possible NULL‑pointer dereferences.

The patch removes a generic vm_xsave_req_perm call from KVM self‑tests, moves it into amx_test, and adds a parameter to select the requested xsave bit, simplifying test setup and allowing future tests to customize the bit.

The patch updates HDMI detection for the hdmi_enable_4kp60 option by replacing clk_round_rate() with clk_get_max_rate() to correctly infer the parameter after a clock subsystem change, restoring 4K@60Hz output.

The patch modifies the hwmon devm registration API so that the 'chip' argument of devm_hwmon_device_register_with_info() must be supplied, preventing callers from omitting or passing NULL, which previously allowed incorrect API conversion.
The patch modifies the lm90 hardware monitoring driver to replace explicit left‑shift expressions with the BIT macro, improving code readability without altering functionality.
The commit overrides the generic module ELF check on powerpc/64 to verify the ELF ABI version, ensuring modules built with the correct ABI (including potential big‑endian ABI V2) are accepted.

The patch replaces simple‑KMS helper functions in the simpledrm driver with the standard DRM atomic helper APIs, removes unused CRTC enable/disable helpers, and always calls drm_atomic_helper_check_plane_state(). No functional behavior changes, only code restructuring for better architecture and reuse.

The patch replaces manual cancellation of a delayed work in the sbs‑charger driver with devm_delayed_work_autocancel(), removing the explicit remove() that called cancel_delayed_work_sync() even when the work was never initialized.
Adds a matching type_clear() call during cleanup for mlx4 devlink ports when type_set() was previously used, fixing missing cleanup.
Adds a JPEG decode worker interface to the MediaTek MT8195 driver, enabling three hardware JPEG decoders to run in parallel.
The patch updates the cdce925 clock driver to use the new i2c simple probe API and i2c_match_id for driver data lookup, removing the old id argument and simplifying probe handling.
The patch replaces a custom delayed‑work implementation in the da9063 driver with the helper devm_delayed_work_autocancel(), reducing code size and leveraging device‑managed cleanup.

The patch moves the keep_towrite handling from ext4_writepage() to ext4_bio_write_page() so pages that cannot write all buffers retain the TOWRITE tag, preventing race‑condition data loss during writeback, especially for transaction‑commit writeback.

Moves snapshot lookup from devlink_nl_region_read_snapshot_fill to devlink_nl_cmd_region_read_dumpit, removes an unused attrs argument, and enables early exit on invalid snapshot IDs, simplifying the code flow.
The commit raises the deprecation delay for SELinux's checkreqprot and runtime‑disable knobs from 5 s to 15 s, making the deprecation notice more visible to users still employing these options.
Updates the gs_usb CAN driver to support up to three CAN‑FD channels per device, aligning the driver with STM32G3 chips that expose three channels.
The patch deletes the unused variable 'found_devs' from the qla2xxx SCSI driver, as it is only incremented and never referenced elsewhere.
The patch deletes several VPRINTK() debug print statements and the ata_scsi_dump_cdb() helper because the same information is already emitted via tracepoints, reducing redundant logging.
The patch corrects a kernel-doc comment in drivers/hv/vmbus_drv.c so the documented prototype matches __vmbus_child_driver_register, removing a compile‑time warning.

The patch removes the mandatory back_lock when getting an iSCSI task, adding logic to detect the final put and only lock when freeing the task, thus reducing contention and improving performance while preserving correctness.

The patch rewrites DRM EDID logging to use device‑specific debug helpers, adds a uniform connector identifier format, passes connector pointers more widely, and condenses tile debug output to a single line.

The patch extracts the post‑delay portion of pci_power_up() into a new helper pci_set_full_power_state(), called only by pci_set_power_state(), while the other caller continues to use pci_power_up() without the redundant work.

The patch updates the i915 driver to drop the Intel Ice Lake (ICL) specific Thunderbolt (TBT) power domain definitions and rename them to match the generic TBT1‑4 naming defined in the hardware specification.
The commit deletes remaining IDE driver documentation files that were left after the driver removal, cleaning up the source tree.
Patch modifies amdgpu_display_framebuffer_init to skip tiling‑flag validation when virtual display (vkms) is enabled, because vkms lacks FB modifier support, eliminating the GFX9+ warning.

The patch adds a hypervisor detection check in ACPICA’s sleep‑state handling and skips the WBINVD cache‑flush when running inside a VM, preventing the #VE exception on TDX guests and eliminating unnecessary flushes.
The patch strengthens tcp_read_sock() by handling unexpected return values from recv_actor(), adding a one‑time warning and ensuring progress to avoid an infinite loop.
The patch changes rhashtable’s internal locking from bh‑safe to irq‑safe, updating lock/unlock helpers to pass flags directly, so the hash table can now be accessed from interrupt context.
Adds an explicit length check before calling memset in vtpm_proxy_fops_read to silence GCC -Warray-bounds warnings and ensure future robustness against potential buffer overflows.

The commit updates the yas530 IIO magnetometer driver to use DEFINE_RUNTIME_DEV_PM_OPS() and pm_ptr() macros, enabling the compiler to drop the dev_pm_ops structure and related functions when CONFIG_PM is disabled, removing the need for __maybe_unused annotations.
Updates RTC driver files to include <linux/kstrtox.h> where kstrto functions are used, reflecting their move from <linux/kernel.h>.

The patch adjusts SDMA engine handling during driver shutdown and resume under SR‑IOV, disabling the engine on hw_fini and re‑enabling it when SR‑IOV is active to avoid premature use before initialization.
The commit adds a generic timeout function interface for the MediaTek JPEG decoder, enabling handling of hardware timeouts and generalizing existing code.
Adds AMD DRM driver support to enter zstate during extended vblank when FreeSync video state provides extra blank lines, calculating gained time and updating registers, restoring defaults on exit.
The commit deletes the ipa_fw_mem node from the trogdor device‑tree because the carveout is unused on trogdor boards and its presence triggers a memory‑region overlap warning at boot.
The commit refactors Btrfs extent I/O tree merging code to replace direct rb_next/rb_prev traversal with the existing next_state/prev_state helper functions, simplifying the logic.

The patch changes the prototype of the hqd_destroy() callback so its third argument type matches the actual implementations (enum kfd_preempt_type → uint32_t), eliminating a CFI type mismatch that caused a kernel panic on certain GPUs.
The patch updates the meson-sm1-odroid device tree to use the correct GPIO pin and set it to open‑drain for the tf‑io regulator, fixing a boot‑loop that occurs after a reboot.

The patch consolidates handling of child events when a parent inode has a mark but the FS_EVENT_ON_CHILD flag is absent. It moves the exclusion logic into the mark‑type iterator preparation, ensuring the parent mark is not considered, which stops incorrect clearing of ignore masks and restores proper event reporting.

The commit adds support for multiple BAR mapping configurations in the NTB endpoint function driver, storing BAR numbers in ntb_epf_data so different devices can select appropriate BAR layouts (config/scratchpad, doorbell, memory windows).

The commit updates the STM32 pinctrl device tree binding by renaming the property from 'reset' to the correct 'resets' and adds 'additionalProperties: false' to the schema, fixing the naming error and tightening validation.
Adds propagation of timestamp socket flags through ping6 so IPv6 ping sockets can return packet timestamps, a capability that was previously unavailable.
Adds a new compatible string for Microchip's Icicle reference design in the RISC‑V dt‑bindings, documenting the FPGA fabric version.

Adds proper error handling in rio_register_mport(): on device_register() failure it calls put_device() to release the allocated name and removes the port from rio_mports list, preventing a resource leak.

The patch separates kernel‑only capability flags from the user‑visible device_cap_flags in the RDMA driver, adds a kernel_cap_flags field, documents each flag, and removes unused flags, clarifying the uapi bitmap.
Commit adds a compiler pragma to silence an array‑bounds warning in ath9k's mac.c for GCC 12, without altering runtime behavior.

The patch updates KVM’s CPUID handling for x86 so that when the base XFD feature flag is not reported, the XFD bits for each state component are cleared, aligning KVM’s CPUID output with Intel’s XFD specification.

Adds explicit #include of linux/highmem.h and linux/swap.h where required in i915 driver, enabling removal of the broad linux/i2c.h include from i915_drv.h that previously pulled those headers indirectly.

Adds a boolean flag in the mlx5 driver to track whether the vport ACL namespace has been created, so it is only allocated once and freed only on driver unload or bare‑metal mode, avoiding unnecessary reallocation when switching eswitch modes.

The commit adds logic for the bq25892 charger driver to read the usb_type property from an external power‑supply device and set the input‑current‑limit (IINLIM) accordingly, enabling charger‑type detection that the chip lacks.
The commit replaces uses of SERIAL_XMIT_SIZE with UART_XMIT_SIZE throughout the serial driver, consolidating the macro name to a single definition.
The patch rewrites the KVM self‑test xapic_ipi_test to create VCPUs with vm_create_with_vcpus() and pass struct kvm_vcpu pointers instead of numeric VCPU IDs, removing role‑specific macros.
Creates nf_nat_ovs.c, moves similar OVS and TC NAT functions there, exports nf_ct_nat() for shared use, and adjusts protocol extraction while keeping OVS/TC‑specific checks separate.
The patch removes direct calls to da7219_aad_jack_det() in the Rockchip ASoC driver and replaces them with the generic component->set_jack() API, enforcing proper abstraction.

The patch deletes a set of AVIC‑related function prototypes from the KVM SVM operation table because their implementations were removed when AVIC was made optional static. No runtime behavior is altered; only dead declarations are cleaned up.

The patch updates the self‑test script test_lirc_mode2.sh to return proper exit codes: non‑zero on execution failure and a skip code when the test is not run, and adds quoting to avoid always‑true condition.
The patch deletes the redundant enum odm_bw from the r8188eu driver, keeping ht_channel_width as the sole definition.

Updates the perf test suite's CSV output linter (test -F 83) to handle the different number of fields on s390 by replacing a Python comma‑counting script with a Bash function, allowing the test to succeed.
Adds an explicit include of the gpiolib header in the Samsung ASoC driver to ensure the code compiles even when the header is not pulled indirectly, avoiding build failures in certain configurations.

The commit updates the AD4130 driver sysfs documentation, reformatting the list of in_voltage-voltage_filter_mode_available modes into a proper bullet list with blank lines to satisfy Sphinx formatting.
Adds support for the RPC‑IF module clock on the R8A779G0 SoC and corrects a table‑alignment typo in the clock definition.

The patch changes the SCSI core to reallocate a device's budget_map after slave_configure() updates the queue depth, ensuring the map size matches the actual hardware limits instead of the static template values.
The patch removes an unnecessary register write in the GV100 init_shader_exceptions() routine of the Nouveau DRM driver to align the implementation with the reference model.
Adds an extensible rseq ABI; kernel now reports supported rseq struct size and alignment via ELF auxiliary vectors, letting user-space register with the original 32‑byte struct or larger ones.
Updates the sun8i-ss crypto driver to replace pm_runtime_get_sync with pm_runtime_resume_and_get, simplifying runtime power‑management handling.
The patch updates two macros in the vt6655 driver, renaming the variable wData to reg_value to comply with lower‑case naming and satisfy checkpatch.pl's CamelCase rule.
The patch refactors the hisi_sas driver so that slave_configure_v3_hw() calls the existing hisi_sas_slave_configure() function, removing duplicated code.
The commit aligns the function amdgpu_ring_init's prototype and definition by renaming parameters in the header from ring_size to max_dw and prio to hw_prio, ensuring both use identical names.
The patch makes the Bluetooth driver always set the event mask after successful disconnects during suspend, avoiding premature wakeups when wakeup is disabled.

Adds a 1 MiB upper bound for OSS period bytes and uses array_size helpers to detect multiplication overflows, preventing vmalloc() from being called with sizes > INT_MAX, thus fixing the overflow reported by syzbot.
Adds support for Quectel EM05-G USB modem in the option driver, handling its two USB configurations (RMNET and MBIM) by defining appropriate interfaces and descriptors.
Adds a Linux power supply driver for the uPI uG3105 battery monitor, handling its coulomb counter and defining a placeholder property for future devicetree support.
The patch updates hugetlb cgroup code to work with folios instead of pages, modifies __remove_hugetlb_page() accordingly, and deletes the unused hugetlb_cgroup_from_page_resv() helper.

The patch modifies the Gaudi2 driver’s hard‑reset sequence, increasing the sleep delay from 500 ms to 2 s so firmware and preboot finish before the driver polls the PSOC BTM_FSM register, preventing premature register access.

The patch modifies the jsa1212 light driver’s i2c remove callback to always return 0, suppressing the i2c core’s redundant error message because the driver already logs failures. It cleans up error handling and readies the code for a future void-return API.

The patch moves the fixed‑file install/remove helpers into the filetable subsystem and changes their signatures to accept a context (ctx) instead of an io_kiocb, reflecting that they operate on the ring rather than a specific request.
Adds an IOCTL interface to enable, disable, and query runtime-configurable firmware features for Xilinx devices.
Adds documentation for the ti,set-io-isolation property in the wkup-m3-ipc device tree bindings, describing its effect on IO isolation during low‑power transitions on am43xx platforms.

The patch modifies the i915 driver to allocate the scratch page in system RAM for all GPU platforms, providing a uniform configuration, freeing device memory, and removing the need for direct device initialization of that page.
The patch disables per‑CPU soft‑irq stacks when PREEMPT_RT is enabled, removing the unused do_softirq_own_stack() path and freeing memory.
The patch updates the ia64 module to replace a hand‑written swap operation with the standard swap() macro from include/linux/minmax.h, simplifying the code and improving readability.

The patch modifies jbd2_submit_inode_data() to call the filesystem's j_submit_inode_data_buffers hook instead of the hard‑coded jbd2_journal_submit_inode_data_buffers, enabling ext4 fastcommits to use ext4_writepages() rather than generic_writepages().
Updates media dt‑bindings for NXP imx8mq VPU, splitting G1 and G2 decoder blocks into separate nodes and noting they are controlled by the vpu‑blk‑ctrl power‑domain, matching the new driver.
Adds a free(soc_dev_attr) call before returning when of_property_read_string() fails in mxs_machine_init(), eliminating a memory leak.

The patch adjusts ov5640_try_frame_interval() to initialize maxfps with the per‑mode max_fps value instead of a hard‑coded 60 fps, ensuring the driver reports the correct maximum frame rate for each sensor mode.
The commit updates the MAINTAINERS file to add Helge Deller as the fbdev subsystem maintainer, reflecting a change in responsibility for that layer.
The patch adjusts whitespace indentation of several lines inside the handle_ctrl_vlan() function in the vdpa/mlx5 driver, aligning them with surrounding code for better readability.
Adds conditional conversion of power values from micro‑Watts to milli‑Watts for SCMI v3.1 in the cpufreq SCMI driver, enabling correct reporting to the Energy Model.
Adds a notifier_block in the random subsystem to inform drivers when a virtual machine forks, with register/unregister helpers; becomes a no‑op when VM‑fork detection is disabled.

The patch deletes the Btrfs extent writepage address‑space operation callback, which was only used for single‑page writeback from kswapd memory reclaim. Since this path is rarely invoked and harms I/O patterns, the code is removed.
The patch deletes a stray comment that was unintentionally introduced for a not‑yet‑implemented feature, restoring the source to its intended state.
The patch renames accesses to the TRCIDR3 register in the etm4x coresight driver to follow the sysreg.h naming convention (REGISTER_FIELD_MASK), improving readability without altering generated code.
The patch moves the PAS operations out of __mdt_load() into a separate helper, allowing callers to invoke PAS directly without changing qcom_mdt_load()'s prototype, improving modularity.
Adds a Chinese translation of the vm/page_frags.rst documentation file in the docs/zh_CN directory.
